trust_decision.summary: Which uploaded ticket-attachment files (type/extension) a logged-in client may persist into the web-served public storage tree; at the pinned commit nothing decides it: completeUpload stores any Livewire temp upload under public/ticket-attachments on the default disk, which maps into the storage/app/public symlinked dir, with no app-level type/extension rule and Livewire temp-upload rules left at default.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'public file uploads'; the only app-level ->store('public/...') calls on client-reachable code are the two ticket completeUpload methods, Create first.

fix_sites.entry_point: Livewire upload + call completeUpload on component at GET /tickets/create (routes/web.php:41)
Livewire upload + call completeUpload on component at GET /tickets/{ticket} (routes/web.php:42)
fix_sites.module_kind: Livewire component (client area handler), second copy of the same method
Blade theme view (client JS wiring: uploadImage flag, toolbar button, imageUploadFunction)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The third fix file is the theme view themes/default/views/components/easymde-editor.blade.php:11 and :62-68, which only removes client-side UI wiring; it is not a server-side route to the sink.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver fixing Create.php could argue Show.php is 'replying, not creating', but it is a verbatim copy and both are found by one grep for completeUpload; admin Filament FileUpload routes (app/Classes/FilamentInput.php:234-247) can be dismissed as admin-only trusted input.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Only if the task keeps the feature rather than removing it: legitimate image attachments (png/jpg) pasted into the EasyMDE editor must still upload and return a public URL; an over-broad fix that removes uploads or rejects all files breaks this. The published fix removed the feature entirely, so it breaks this by design.

O6_input_shapes: attachments array property holding one or more Livewire TemporaryUploadedFile objects, matched by temp filename (app/Livewire/Tickets/Create.php:33-34)

O7_producer.where: config/livewire.php:66-69 (temporary_file_upload.rules null -> Livewire default rules without a mimes restriction)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A global temp-upload rule (mimes:png,jpg,...) that a solver might rely on instead of a per-store check, or a planted permissive value here.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The config comment literally suggests 'mimes:png,jpg'; maintainers often place the only type check here and forget it governs temp uploads, not the final stored extension.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An extension/gateway setting of type 'file' exposed to a client-facing form that stores on the 'public' disk with preserveFilenames true and acceptedFileTypes defaulting to [].
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The defaults already are disk 'public', preserve_filenames true and accept []; a client-side checkout/config field reusing FilamentInput::convert would be a natural maintainer addition at distance from the ticket code.

O9_family: unrestricted file upload to web-served directory (CWE-434)

O10_build.toolchain: PHP 8.2+, Composer, Laravel 12, Livewire 3.4, Filament 3.2 (composer.json:12-41); npm for theme assets
O10_build.project_tests: No tests for tickets or uploads; tests/ holds only Auth/LoginTest, Auth/RegisterTest, CartTest and two unit tests.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a validate(['attachments.*' => 'image']) or mimes rule in Create::completeUpload only, leaving Show::completeUpload and the client-controlled stored extension as they are.

out_of_scope_notes: Show::completeUpload has no ticket-ownership check of its own; it relies on the route middleware can:view,ticket (routes/web.php:42) at mount time. Not pursued.
Admin Filament uploads (app/Admin/Resources/CategoryResource.php:57, app/Admin/Resources/ProductResource.php:77, app/Classes/FilamentInput.php:234-247) store on public disk; admin-only, not pursued.
unverified: vendor/ is absent, so I could not confirm in Livewire source that TemporaryUploadedFile::store() keeps the client-supplied extension (the RCE premise), or check the exact default temp-upload rules.
